paras: The beating of W. M. Herdon was an assault on a Black man by a white man and a street crowd at First avenue S and Third street, apparently in Minneapolis, Minnesota, at about 1 a.m. on August 15, 1905. Herdon was severely beaten and then arrested by police for disorderly conduct, while no attacker is reported to have been held. The Minneapolis Journal's brief item framed the crowd as having helped "punish" a "colored man" for drawing a knife.

According to the Journal, Herdon, described as "a colored man," and a young white man had a dispute, during which the paper said Herdon attacked the young man with a knife. The white man, "much the smaller" of the two, threw Herdon to the ground and was beating him when the crowd that had gathered joined in. The paper gave no source for the knife accusation and did not describe Herdon's injuries beyond calling him "severely beaten."

The white man then left the scene, and police arrested Herdon on a charge of disorderly conduct. No report of the outcome of the charge, or of any arrest of the white man or members of the crowd, appears in the coverage.

The episode is known from a single unsigned local item on page 4 of the Minneapolis Journal on the day of the beating. Under the headline "Crowd Jumped On" and the deck "Helped Punish Colored Man for Drawing a Knife," the paper stated the knife attack as fact and cast the crowd's beating as punishment. Its text set "a colored man" against "the white man," naming the race of both men, and named only Herdon.
No other white paper and no Black paper was found to have reported the beating.
